name: LF398MX_NOPB
title: LF198-N, LF298, LF398-N, LF198A-N, LF398A-N monolithic sample-and-hold circuits
summary: A one-chip sample-and-hold amplifier: a bipolar input amplifier drives an external hold capacitor through a switch, and a JFET-input output buffer follows the capacitor voltage, so the whole works as a unity-gain follower. A differential logic input with a 1.4 V threshold chooses sample (logic high) or hold (logic low). It runs from ±5 V to ±18 V. The grades differ in temperature range and limits: LF198-N and LF198A-N for −55 °C to 125 °C, LF298 for −25 °C to 85 °C, LF398-N and LF398A-N for 0 °C to 70 °C; the A versions carry tighter limits. Packages are 14-pin SOIC, 8-pin TO-99 and 8-pin PDIP.

operation.text: A bipolar input op amp with 30 kΩ feedback from the output and a pair of back-to-back clamp diodes drives the hold-capacitor node through a switch. The switch is opened and closed by a differential comparator on LOGIC and LOGIC REFERENCE. The Ch pin reaches the switch through an internal 300 Ω resistor. A JFET-input output amplifier buffers the capacitor node and closes the loop to the input amplifier, giving unity gain overall.

LOGIC above LOGIC REFERENCE selects sample: the output tracks the input while the hold capacitor charges and discharges. LOGIC below LOGIC REFERENCE selects hold: the input is cut off and the output keeps the capacitor voltage. A smaller capacitor tracks faster signals; a larger one droops more slowly.

Input impedance is about 10^10 Ω. The input characteristics are the same in sample and hold, and input signals as large as the supply voltages do not feed through to the output in hold. Bandwidth is wide enough for the part to sit inside the loop of a 1 MHz op amp and stay stable. Acquisition to 0.01 % can be as short as 6 µs.

LOGIC and LOGIC REFERENCE form a differential input with low input current and a 1.4 V threshold, so TTL, PMOS and CMOS drive it directly. Higher logic levels and op amp drive use the divider networks of the logic drive table, which move the threshold.

The logic edge must slew at no less than 1.0 V/µs; slower edges make the hold step large. With an RC delay ahead of the logic input, the slope at the threshold crossing must still be at least 1.0 V/µs.

The capacitor value trades hold step against acquisition time and droop; size and cost grow with value. Fast repetition or fast tracking makes the capacitor currents heat the chip noticeably. Dielectric absorption is a major error: Mylar can recover by up to 0.2 % after a fast step and needs long sample times. Polystyrene, polypropylene and Teflon have very low hysteresis; mica and polycarbonate are worse; most ceramics exceed 1 %. Polypropylene raises the usable ambient from 85 °C (polystyrene) to 100 °C. NPO/COG ceramics work to 125 °C with low absorption. Polypropylene relaxes with a 10 ms to 50 ms time constant, so converting within 1 ms of the hold command cuts the hysteresis error about tenfold.

OFFSET ADJUST goes to the wiper of a 1 kΩ potentiometer whose one end is at V+ and whose other end returns to ground through a resistor chosen for about 0.6 mA in the potentiometer. Trimming this pin leaves the offset drift unchanged.

An inverter driven from the logic signal feeds a potentiometer connected between its input and output; 10 pF from the wiper to the hold capacitor gives about ±4 mV of hold-step trim with a 0.01 µF capacitor and 5 V logic. Larger logic swings call for less than 10 pF.

The analog path lags the input, and the capacitor lags a little more through the 300 Ω on-chip resistor, while logic delay acts the other way. Example: a 20 Vp-p, 10 kHz input slews at up to 0.6 V/µs; 100 ns of logic delay gives up to +60 mV, while a 1 MHz analog loop (160 ns lag) gives −96 mV, a net −36 mV. Analog delay grows with hold capacitance; logic delay does not. The aperture time curve is based on a 1 mV error at the output; the hold settling curve gives the time to settle within 1 mV.

Fast logic edges coupling into the analog input at the moment of hold cause hold errors. Keep logic traces far from both the Ch pin and the analog input, guard the input line with grounded traces when it comes from a high impedance, and keep logic swing near 2.5 V. A guard ring around Ch, connected to the output, works with a 10-pin layout.

Rated at ±15 V typical. Bypass each supply with about 0.1 µF ceramic near the pin plus 10 µF or more tantalum or ceramic; the large capacitor may serve several devices. Capacitors must be rated for the supply voltage.

Keep the bypass loop between supply pins and ground small, place a ground plane under the part with a via close to each bypass capacitor, put the bypass capacitors next to their pins on wide traces, and keep feedback parts close to the device.

Hold step: output step on going from sample to hold with a DC input and 5 V logic swing. Acquisition time: time to acquire a new input with a 10 V output step, including settling of internal nodes so the held value is right. Gain error: percent difference between output swing and input swing in sample mode. Hold settling time: time for the output to settle within 1 mV after the hold command. Dynamic sampling error: held-output error caused by a moving input at the hold command, given in mV for a hold capacitor and slew rate. Aperture time: delay needed between the hold command and an input transition so that the transition leaves the held value alone.
ESD protection is limited; store and handle with leads shorted or in conductive foam.

circuits.title: Typical connection
circuits.description: The basic follower: the signal goes to INPUT, the hold capacitor Ch from the Ch pin to ground, LOGIC REFERENCE to ground and the logic signal to LOGIC. A 5 V level samples and 0 V holds.

parts.value: logic input (5 V sample, 0 V hold)

circuits.title: Sample when logic high with TTL and CMOS biasing
circuits.description: For logic highs of 3 V to 7 V: LOGIC REFERENCE is grounded and the logic signal drives LOGIC directly, so a high samples. Threshold 1.4 V.

circuits.title: Sample when logic low with TTL and CMOS biasing
circuits.description: For logic highs of 3 V to 7 V with inverted sense: R1 from V+ and R2 (5.6k) to ground hold LOGIC at 2.8 V, and the logic signal drives LOGIC REFERENCE, so a low samples. R1 is chosen to set the 2.8 V. Threshold 1.4 V.

circuits.title: Sample when logic high with CMOS biasing
circuits.description: For CMOS highs of 7 V to 15 V: 20k from V+ and 30k to ground bias LOGIC REFERENCE at 0.4 of V+, and the logic signal drives LOGIC, so a high samples. Threshold 0.6 (V+) + 1.4 V.

circuits.title: Sample when logic low with CMOS biasing
circuits.description: For CMOS highs of 7 V to 15 V with inverted sense: 30k from V+ and 20k to ground bias LOGIC, and the logic signal drives LOGIC REFERENCE, so a low samples. Threshold 0.6 (V+) − 1.4 V.

circuits.title: Sample when logic high with operational amplifier biasing
circuits.description: An op amp swinging ±13 V drives LOGIC through an 8.2k / 4.7k divider to ground; LOGIC REFERENCE is grounded, so the positive swing samples. Threshold about +4 V.

parts.value: op amp drive, +13 V sample, −13 V hold

circuits.title: Sample when logic low with operational amplifier biasing
circuits.description: The same ±13 V drive and 8.2k / 4.7k divider go to LOGIC REFERENCE, with LOGIC grounded, so the negative swing samples. Threshold −4 V.

parts.value: op amp drive, +13 V hold, −13 V sample

circuits.title: X1000 sample and hold
circuits.description: Gain of about 1000 inside the sample-and-hold: an LM108 takes VIN at its noninverting input, with R3 (1 MΩ) from the LF198 output and R4 (1 kΩ) to ground at its inverting input, for a noninverting gain of 1001, and drives the LF198 INPUT. Two antiparallel 1N457 diodes join the LF198 output to LM108 pin 8. A 100k potentiometer between +15 V and −15 V feeds the inverting node through R2 (2M) for offset adjust. C1 ≈ 100/AV pF from COMP 2 to ground; at this gain it is 0.1 pF and is left off, and lower gains need the LM108 compensated.

parts.note: optional; needed only for lower gains

notes: The supply connections of both ICs are not specified.

circuits.title: Sample and difference circuit
circuits.description: VIN reaches the Ch pin through 0.01 µF and 1k, and INPUT is grounded or taken to VB. The logic input selects reset (high) or track (low). In hold mode the output follows the input: VOUT = VB + ΔVIN.

parts.value: VB, optional, in place of ground

notes: INPUT is grounded when no VB is used.
The supply connections are not specified.

circuits.title: Ramp generator with variable reset level
circuits.description: R1 (8.2k) from 15 V feeds the cathode of an LM113 1.2 V reference whose anode is the output; R2 runs from that node to the Ch pin and Ch. The rise or fall rate is 1.2 V / (R2 × Ch). The reset input at 5 V samples the reset level input; at 0 V the output ramps.

circuits.title: Integrator with programmable reset level
circuits.description: An LF398 with an LM308: Ch at the LF398 Ch pin is also the LM308 noninverting input node, which takes the + integrating input through R1 (1M) and the LM308 output through R2 (200k). The inverting input takes the − integrating input through R3 (1M) and the LM308 output through R4 (200k). The LM308 has 100 pF from pin 8 to ground. The reset level VR goes to the LF398 INPUT and the reset/integrate pulse to LOGIC; in hold mode VOUT = (1 / (R1 × Ch)) ∫ VIN dt + VR.
notes: The VR input node also carries a ground connection.

circuits.title: Output holds at average of sampled input
circuits.description: Rh in series with the hold capacitor, from the Ch pin to ground, makes the output hold at the average of the sampled input; choose Rh × Ch ≫ 1 / (2π fIN(min)).

circuits.title: Increased slew current
circuits.description: Two 1N457 diodes in inverse parallel between OUTPUT and the Ch pin raise the slew current into the hold capacitor.
notes: The supply and logic connections are not specified.

circuits.title: Reset stabilized amplifier
circuits.description: An LH0042H amplifier with 1M from its output and 1k to ground at the inverting input, for a gain of 1000. The input reaches its noninverting input through a 2N5116 JFET whose gate is driven from the reset pulse through 30k; 12k joins the two amplifier inputs. The LF398 samples the amplifier output on reset pulses of 2 ms or more, and its output returns through 200k to LH0042H pin 5; pin 1 has 200k to ground. The hold capacitor is 0.033 µF in series with 4.7k. VOS ≤ 20 µV without trim; ZIN ≈ 1 MΩ.
notes: ΔVOS/Δt ≈ 30 µV/s and ΔVOS/ΔT ≈ 0.1 µV/°C.
Q1 pins: G gate; D toward the input, S toward the amplifier.

circuits.title: Fast acquisition, low droop sample and hold
circuits.description: Two LF398s in cascade: the first, with 0.002 µF, takes the input; the second, with 1 µF, takes the first one's output and drives the output. A 10 µs sample pulse drives the first LF398 LOGIC and triggers an LM3905 timer (1.2M and 0.01 µF timing, supply 5 V to 15 V); the timer output, with 3.3k to ground, gives a 12 ms pulse to the second LF398 LOGIC.

circuits.title: Synchronous correlator for recovering signals below noise level
circuits.description: Two LM122H timers make the sample pulse: the first is triggered by the synchronous clock and its timing capacitor C2 is charged from 15 V through a PNP transistor and R2 (1M); its output (pin 9, 12k pull-up) triggers the second, which gives a 10 µs pulse (20k and 470 pF timing, 10k from 15 V and 4.7k to ground on its output, with pin 10 grounded) to the LF198 LOGIC. The LF198 with 1000 pF samples the signal input and R1 (47k) with C1 filters its output. The output frequency is set by the sweep rate. C1 is selected to filter the lowest frequency component of the input noise; C2 ≈ 5 × 10^−6 / fIN. R3, from timer pin 6 (500 Ω to ground), goes to the scope sweep and is scaled for about 0 V to 3 V at pin 6.

parts.note: chosen to filter the lowest frequency part of the input noise

circuits.title: 2-channel switch
circuits.description: INPUT is channel A, and the Ch pin, through R1 (47k), is channel B. The select input at 5 V picks A and at 0 V picks B.

circuits.title: DC and AC zeroing
circuits.description: DC zero: OFFSET ADJUST takes the wiper of a 1k potentiometer between 15 V and a 24k resistor to ground. AC (hold step) zero: an inverter on the logic line, a 10k potentiometer from its input to its output, and 10 pF from that wiper to the Ch pin.
notes: The V− connection is not specified.

circuits.title: Staircase generator
circuits.description: Two LF398s, a 2N2222 and an LM113 1.2 V reference. The clock reaches the LOGIC pin of U1 through R3 (4.7k) with D1 and 300 pF, and the LOGIC REFERENCE pin of U2 through R7 (4.7k) with D2 and 300 pF; U2 LOGIC is biased from 15 V by R8 (12k) and R9 (3k). U1 INPUT takes the output of U2 through R2 (47k). U2 INPUT takes the output through R6, and from the LM113 node (fed from 15 V by R4, 8.2k) through R5 (11k). The output steps up from 0 V; R6 sets the step height, 50 kΩ for a 1 V step. The reset input drives Q1 through R1 (4.7k), and Q1 pulls U1 INPUT to ground.

parts.note: selected for step height: 50 kΩ gives a 1 V step

circuits.title: Differential hold
circuits.description: Two LF198s share LOGIC and LOGIC REFERENCE (grounded). The hold capacitor joins the two Ch pins, and the second Ch pin has 100k to ground. VS sits between the two INPUT pins, and VCM from the second INPUT to ground. The output is VS in hold mode and VS + VCM in sample mode; the second output is not connected.
notes: The supply connections are not specified.

circuits.title: Capacitor hysteresis compensation
circuits.description: The hold capacitor returns to ground through R3, a 200 Ω trimmer. The output feeds that node through R1 (200k) and R2 (200k), with C1 (0.2 µF) from their junction to ground. C1 is selected for the time constant, C1 = τ / 100 kΩ; R3 is adjusted for amplitude.

circuits.title: Schematic example, SOIC-14
circuits.description: The SOIC-14 part wired for a board: each supply has 10 µF and 0.1 µF to ground, the hold capacitor CH goes from pin 8 to ground, and INPUT, OUTPUT, OFFSET ADJUST, LOGIC, LOGIC REFERENCE and Ch are brought out. The NC pins are left open.
notes: The board layout puts C1 and C2 beside pins 1 to 7, C3 and C4 beside pins 8 to 14, and CH just below pin 8.
